name: Build and Test

on:
  push:
    branches:
      - main
  pull_request:
    branches:
      - main

permissions:
  contents: read

env:
  ROLLUP_SKIP_NODEJS_NATIVE_BUILD: "true"
  FORCE_JAVASCRIPT_ACTIONS_TO_NODE24: "true"

jobs:
  upload-source-event:
    name: Upload source event
    if: github.event_name == 'pull_request'
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    steps:
      - name: Upload source event
        uses: actions/upload-artifact@043fb46d1a93c77aae656e7c1c64a875d1fc6a0a # v7.0.1
        with:
          name: source-event
          path: ${{ github.event_path }}
          if-no-files-found: error

  build:
    name: Build and test (Node ${{ matrix.node-version }})
    runs-on: ubuntu-24.04
    strategy:
      fail-fast: false
      matrix:
        node-version:
          - "24.x"
          - "26.x"

    steps:
      - name: Checkout repository
        uses: actions/checkout@3d3c42e5aac5ba805825da76410c181273ba90b1 # v7.0.1
        with:
          fetch-depth: 0
          persist-credentials: false

      - name: Set up Node.js
        uses: actions/setup-node@820762786026740c76f36085b0efc47a31fe5020 # v7.0.0
        with:
          node-version: ${{ matrix.node-version }}
          cache: "npm"

      - name: Set up mise
        uses: jdx/mise-action@7e36c90d9ab29c415a2384db3006f3ec8a8cc654 # v4.2.4

      - name: Install dependencies
        run: npm ci

      - name: Verify commit messages
        if: github.event_name == 'pull_request' && matrix.node-version == '24.x'
        run: npx commitlint --from ${{ github.event.pull_request.base.sha }} --to ${{ github.event.pull_request.head.sha }} --verbose

      - name: Check for changeset
        if: >-
          github.event_name == 'pull_request' &&
          matrix.node-version == '24.x' &&
          github.actor != 'dependabot[bot]' &&
          github.head_ref != 'changeset-release/main'
        env:
          BASE_REF: ${{ github.base_ref }}
        run: |
          npx changeset status --since="origin/${BASE_REF}"
          npx nx run repository:check:package-changesets -- --since "origin/${BASE_REF}"

      - name: Run Node 26 build
        if: matrix.node-version == '26.x'
        run: npx nx run repository:build
        env:
          SENTRY_ORG: ${{ secrets.SENTRY_ORG }}
          SENTRY_PROJECT: ${{ secrets.SENTRY_PROJECT }}
          SENTRY_AUTH_TOKEN: ${{ secrets.SENTRY_AUTH_TOKEN }}
          OTEL_COLLECTOR_TOKEN: ${{ secrets.OTEL_COLLECTOR_TOKEN }}
          CODECOV_TOKEN: ${{ matrix.node-version == '24.x' && secrets.CODECOV_TOKEN || '' }}

      - name: Run Node 24 validation graph
        if: ${{ !cancelled() && matrix.node-version == '24.x' }}
        env:
          HEVY_API_KEY: ""
          HEVY_TEST_REPORT_MODE: ci
        run: >-
          npx nx run-many --projects=repository --targets=test:unit,check:types,check,check:boundaries,test:worker-http,test:mcp,test:contract,test:cli,worker:dry-run,check:control-plane,check:exports,test:worker --parallel=3 --outputStyle=stream --excludeTaskDependencies

      - name: Run Node 26 validation graph
        if: ${{ !cancelled() && matrix.node-version == '26.x' }}
        env:
          HEVY_TEST_REPORT_MODE: ci
        run: >-
          npx nx run-many --projects=repository --targets=check:control-plane,check:boundaries,check:exports,check:types,check:server-manifest,check,test:mcp,test:unit --parallel=3 --outputStyle=stream

      - name: Upload test results to Codecov
        if: ${{ !cancelled() && matrix.node-version == '24.x' }}
        uses: codecov/codecov-action@fb8b3582c8e4def4969c97caa2f19720cb33a72f # v7.0.0
        with:
          token: ${{ secrets.CODECOV_TOKEN }}
          files: ./test-results/unit-tests.xml
          disable_search: true
          report_type: test_results

      - name: Upload unit test results
        if: ${{ !cancelled() && matrix.node-version == '24.x' }}
        uses: actions/upload-artifact@043fb46d1a93c77aae656e7c1c64a875d1fc6a0a # v7.0.1
        with:
          name: unit-test-results-node-24
          path: test-results/unit-tests.xml
          if-no-files-found: warn

      - name: Upload results to Codecov
        if: matrix.node-version == '24.x'
        uses: codecov/codecov-action@fb8b3582c8e4def4969c97caa2f19720cb33a72f # v7.0.0
        with:
          token: ${{ secrets.CODECOV_TOKEN }}
          files: ./coverage/unit/lcov.info,./coverage/mocked/lcov.info

  package-performance:
    name: Package and performance (Node 24.x)
    runs-on: ubuntu-24.04
    steps:
      - name: Checkout repository
        uses: actions/checkout@3d3c42e5aac5ba805825da76410c181273ba90b1 # v7.0.1
        with:
          fetch-depth: 0
          persist-credentials: false

      - name: Set up Node.js
        uses: actions/setup-node@820762786026740c76f36085b0efc47a31fe5020 # v7.0.0
        with:
          node-version: "24.x"
          cache: "npm"

      - name: Set up mise
        uses: jdx/mise-action@7e36c90d9ab29c415a2384db3006f3ec8a8cc654 # v4.2.4

      - name: Install dependencies
        run: npm ci

      - name: Build package candidate
        run: npx nx run repository:build
        env:
          SENTRY_ORG: ${{ secrets.SENTRY_ORG }}
          SENTRY_PROJECT: ${{ secrets.SENTRY_PROJECT }}
          SENTRY_AUTH_TOKEN: ${{ secrets.SENTRY_AUTH_TOKEN }}
          OTEL_COLLECTOR_TOKEN: ${{ secrets.OTEL_COLLECTOR_TOKEN }}
          CODECOV_TOKEN: ${{ secrets.CODECOV_TOKEN }}

      - name: Prepare shared package candidates
        if: ${{ !cancelled() }}
        run: |
          npx nx run @chrisdoc/hevy-cli:build
          npx nx run repository:check:server-manifest
          npx nx run repository:pack:artifacts --excludeTaskDependencies

      - name: Run isolated performance validation
        if: ${{ !cancelled() }}
        env:
          HEVY_API_KEY: ""
        run: npx nx run repository:test:performance --excludeTaskDependencies

      - name: Run package validation graph
        if: ${{ !cancelled() }}
        env:
          HEVY_API_KEY: ""
        run: >-
          npx nx run-many --projects=repository --targets=test:diagnostics,test:stdio,test:pack,test:pack:cli,check:publint --parallel=3 --outputStyle=stream --excludeTaskDependencies

      - name: Upload performance summary
        if: ${{ always() }}
        uses: actions/upload-artifact@043fb46d1a93c77aae656e7c1c64a875d1fc6a0a # v7.0.1
        with:
          name: performance-summary-node-24
          path: test-results/performance/summary.json
          if-no-files-found: error

  docker:
    name: Build and smoke test Docker image
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    steps:
      - name: Checkout repository
        uses: actions/checkout@3d3c42e5aac5ba805825da76410c181273ba90b1 # v7.0.1
        with:
          persist-credentials: false

      - name: Set up Docker Buildx
        uses: docker/setup-buildx-action@bb05f3f5519dd87d3ba754cc423b652a5edd6d2c # v4.2.0

      - name: Build Docker image
        uses: docker/build-push-action@53b7df96c91f9c12dcc8a07bcb9ccacbed38856a # v7.3.0
        with:
          context: .
          load: true
          tags: hevy-mcp:ci
          cache-from: type=gha,scope=hevy-mcp-ci
          cache-to: type=gha,mode=max,scope=hevy-mcp-ci,ignore-error=true

      - name: Smoke test version output without an API key
        run: docker run --rm hevy-mcp:ci --version

      - name: Smoke test help output without an API key
        run: docker run --rm hevy-mcp:ci --help

      - name: Verify hardened runtime structure
        run: |
          docker run --rm --entrypoint sh hevy-mcp:ci -c '
            test "$(id -u)" -ne 0 &&
            test ! -e /app/node_modules &&
            test -f /app/standalone.mjs
          '

  otel-cicd-action:
    if: always()
    name: OpenTelemetry Export Trace
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    needs: [build, package-performance, docker]
    env:
      OTEL_COLLECTOR_TOKEN: ${{ secrets.OTEL_COLLECTOR_TOKEN }}
    steps:
      - name: Export workflow
        # The collector token exists only in chrisdoc/hevy-mcp, and fork PRs
        # run without secrets — skip the export when the token is absent
        # instead of failing the whole workflow.
        if: env.OTEL_COLLECTOR_TOKEN != ''
        uses: corentinmusard/otel-cicd-action@6022e68732c1cab4d2c8218b810f69006ee5cc34 # v4.1.0
        with:
          otlpEndpoint: "https://otel.chrisdoc.dev/v1/traces"
          otlpHeaders: "Authorization=Bearer ${{ env.OTEL_COLLECTOR_TOKEN }}"
          githubToken: ${{ secrets.GITHUB_TOKEN }}
          runId: ${{ github.run_id }}

content.text:
name: Release

on:
  # This privileged follow-up is gated to a successful push to main from this
  # repository, so it only checks out a trusted commit already tested by CI.
  workflow_run: # zizmor: ignore[dangerous-triggers]
    workflows: ["Build and Test"]
    types: [completed]
    branches: [main]
permissions: {}

env:
  ROLLUP_SKIP_NODEJS_NATIVE_BUILD: "true"
  FORCE_JAVASCRIPT_ACTIONS_TO_NODE24: "true"

jobs:
  release:
    if: >-
      github.event.workflow_run.conclusion == 'success' &&
      github.event.workflow_run.event == 'push' &&
      github.event.workflow_run.head_branch == 'main' &&
      github.event.workflow_run.head_repository.full_name == github.repository
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    permissions:
      contents: write # to be able to publish a GitHub release
      issues: write # to be able to comment on released issues
      pull-requests: write # to be able to comment on released pull requests
      id-token: write # to enable use of OIDC for npm provenance
    outputs:
      version: ${{ steps.release.outputs.version }}
      released: ${{ steps.release.outputs.released }}
      node_released: ${{ steps.release.outputs.node_released }}
      worker_version: ${{ steps.release.outputs.worker_version }}
      worker_released: ${{ steps.release.outputs.worker_released }}
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@3d3c42e5aac5ba805825da76410c181273ba90b1 # v7.0.1
        with:
          fetch-depth: 0
          ref: ${{ github.event.workflow_run.head_sha }}
          persist-credentials: false
      - uses: actions/setup-node@820762786026740c76f36085b0efc47a31fe5020 # v7.0.0
        with:
          node-version-file: ".nvmrc"
          cache: "npm"
      - run: npm ci
      - name: Build release package
        run: npx nx run repository:build
        env:
          HEVY_MCP_RELEASE: "true"
          SENTRY_ORG: ${{ secrets.SENTRY_ORG }}
          SENTRY_PROJECT: ${{ secrets.SENTRY_PROJECT }}
          SENTRY_AUTH_TOKEN: ${{ secrets.SENTRY_AUTH_TOKEN }}
          OTEL_COLLECTOR_TOKEN: ${{ secrets.OTEL_COLLECTOR_TOKEN }}
      - name: Prepare shared package candidates
        run: |
          npx nx run @chrisdoc/hevy-cli:build
          npx nx run repository:check:server-manifest
          npx nx run repository:pack:artifacts --excludeTaskDependencies
      - name: Validate release candidates
        run: >-
          npx nx run-many --projects=repository --targets=test:release-unit,test:worker,test:pack,test:cli,test:pack:cli,check:publint --parallel=3 --outputStyle=stream --excludeTaskDependencies
      - name: Run integration tests
        run: npx nx run repository:test:integration
        env:
          HEVY_API_KEY: ${{ secrets.HEVY_API_KEY }}

      - name: Test source MCP build
        run: npx nx run repository:test:nightly
        env:
          HEVY_API_KEY: ${{ secrets.HEVY_API_KEY }}
          HEVY_MCP_COMMAND: node
          HEVY_MCP_ARGS_JSON: '["packages/node/dist/cli.mjs"]'
          HEVY_MCP_LAUNCHER: release-source
          HEVY_MCP_SOURCE_REVISION: ${{ github.sha }}
          HEVY_MCP_DIAGNOSTICS_PATH: test-results/release-source.json

      - name: Smoke test live local Worker HTTP path
        continue-on-error: true
        run: npx nx run repository:test:worker-http:live
        env:
          HEVY_API_KEY: ${{ secrets.HEVY_API_KEY }}
          HEVY_RUN_LIVE_WORKER_TESTS: "1"

      - name: Create Release PR or Publish
        id: changesets
        uses: changesets/action@2d9f7af6402422be60d377f151c7618011bba45a # v2.0.0-next.4
        with:
          version-script: npx nx run repository:version:changesets
          publish-script: npx nx run repository:release
          commit-message: "chore: version packages"
          pr-title: "chore: version packages"
          github-token: ${{ secrets.GITHUB_TOKEN }}
        env:
          GITHUB_TOKEN: ${{ secrets.GITHUB_TOKEN }}
          SENTRY_ORG: ${{ secrets.SENTRY_ORG }}
          SENTRY_PROJECT: ${{ secrets.SENTRY_PROJECT }}
          SENTRY_AUTH_TOKEN: ${{ secrets.SENTRY_AUTH_TOKEN }}
          OTEL_COLLECTOR_TOKEN: ${{ secrets.OTEL_COLLECTOR_TOKEN }}
          HEVY_MCP_RELEASE: "true"
      - name: Set Release Outputs
        id: release
        env:
          PKGS: ${{ steps.changesets.outputs['published-packages'] }}
          PUBLISHED: ${{ steps.changesets.outputs.published }}
          RELEASE_COMMIT: ${{ github.event.workflow_run.head_sha || github.sha }}
        run: |
          set -euo pipefail
          node scripts/release-outputs.mjs \
            "$RELEASE_COMMIT^1" \
            "$RELEASE_COMMIT" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"

  publish-container:
    name: Publish Docker image
    needs: release
    if: needs.release.outputs.node_released == 'true'
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    permissions:
      contents: read
      packages: write
    steps:
      - name: Checkout tested release commit
        uses: actions/checkout@3d3c42e5aac5ba805825da76410c181273ba90b1 # v7.0.1
        with:
          ref: ${{ github.event.workflow_run.head_sha }}
          persist-credentials: false

      - name: Set up QEMU
        uses: docker/setup-qemu-action@96fe6ef7f33517b61c61be40b68a1882f3264fb8 # v4.2.0

      - name: Set up Docker Buildx
        uses: docker/setup-buildx-action@bb05f3f5519dd87d3ba754cc423b652a5edd6d2c # v4.2.0

      - name: Log in to GitHub Container Registry
        uses: docker/login-action@dbcb813823bdd20940b903addbd779551569679f # v4.6.0
        with:
          registry: ghcr.io
          username: ${{ github.actor }}
          password: ${{ secrets.GITHUB_TOKEN }}

      - name: Generate Docker image metadata
        id: metadata
        uses: docker/metadata-action@dc802804100637a589fabce1cb79ff13a1411302 # v6.2.0
        with:
          images: ghcr.io/${{ github.repository }}
          flavor: latest=false
          tags: |
            type=raw,value=latest,enable=${{ !contains(needs.release.outputs.version, '-') }}
            type=semver,pattern={{version}},value=${{ needs.release.outputs.version }}
            type=semver,pattern={{major}},value=${{ needs.release.outputs.version }}
            type=semver,pattern={{major}}.{{minor}},value=${{ needs.release.outputs.version }}

      - name: Build and publish Docker image
        uses: docker/build-push-action@53b7df96c91f9c12dcc8a07bcb9ccacbed38856a # v7.3.0
        with:
          context: .
          platforms: linux/amd64,linux/arm64
          push: true
          tags: ${{ steps.metadata.outputs.tags }}
          labels: ${{ steps.metadata.outputs.labels }}

  deploy-production:
    name: Deploy production Worker
    needs: release
    if: >-
      github.event.workflow_run.event == 'push' &&
      github.event.workflow_run.head_branch == 'main' &&
      needs.release.outputs.worker_released == 'true'
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    concurrency:
      group: cloudflare-worker-production
      cancel-in-progress: false
    permissions:
      contents: read
    environment:
      name: production
      url: https://hevy.chrisdoc.dev/mcp
    steps:
      - name: Checkout published release commit
        uses: actions/checkout@3d3c42e5aac5ba805825da76410c181273ba90b1 # v7.0.1
        with:
          ref: ${{ github.event.workflow_run.head_sha }}
          persist-credentials: false

      - name: Set up Node.js
        uses: actions/setup-node@820762786026740c76f36085b0efc47a31fe5020 # v7.0.0
        with:
          node-version-file: .nvmrc
          cache: npm

      - name: Install dependencies
        run: npm ci

      - name: Deploy published version
        env:
          CLOUDFLARE_ACCOUNT_ID: ${{ secrets.CLOUDFLARE_ACCOUNT_ID }}
          CLOUDFLARE_API_TOKEN: ${{ secrets.CLOUDFLARE_API_TOKEN }}
          WRANGLER_MODE: production
          CLOUDFLARE_WORKER_NAME: ${{ vars.CLOUDFLARE_WORKER_NAME }}
          CLOUDFLARE_WORKER_ROUTE: ${{ vars.CLOUDFLARE_WORKER_ROUTE }}
          CLOUDFLARE_OTEL_LOGS_DESTINATIONS: ${{ vars.CLOUDFLARE_OTEL_LOGS_DESTINATIONS }}
          CLOUDFLARE_OTEL_TRACES_DESTINATIONS: ${{ vars.CLOUDFLARE_OTEL_TRACES_DESTINATIONS }}
          CLOUDFLARE_OAUTH_KV_NAMESPACE_ID: ${{ secrets.CLOUDFLARE_OAUTH_KV_NAMESPACE_ID }}
          RELEASE_COMMIT: ${{ github.event.workflow_run.head_sha || github.sha }}
          WORKER_VERSION: ${{ needs.release.outputs.worker_version }}
        run: >-
          npx wrangler deploy
          --x-new-config
          --env production
          --tag "$WORKER_VERSION"
          --message "Changesets release at $RELEASE_COMMIT"

  publish-preview:
    name: Publish hevy-mcp preview
    if: >-
      github.event.workflow_run.conclusion == 'success' &&
      github.event.workflow_run.event == 'push' &&
      github.event.workflow_run.head_branch == 'main' &&
      github.event.workflow_run.head_repository.full_name == github.repository
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    concurrency:
      group: npm-preview-main
      cancel-in-progress: true
    permissions:
      contents: read
      id-token: write
    steps:
      - name: Checkout tested commit
        uses: actions/checkout@3d3c42e5aac5ba805825da76410c181273ba90b1 # v7.0.1
        with:
          ref: main
          persist-credentials: false

      - name: Verify tested commit is current main
        env:
          TESTED_SHA: ${{ github.event.workflow_run.head_sha }}
        run: |
          set -euo pipefail
          checked_out_sha="$(git rev-parse HEAD)"
          current_main_sha="$(git ls-remote origin refs/heads/main | awk 'NR == 1 { print $1 }')"
          if [ -z "$current_main_sha" ]; then
            echo "Unable to determine the current origin/main SHA"
            exit 1
          fi
          if [ "$checked_out_sha" != "$TESTED_SHA" ] || [ "$current_main_sha" != "$TESTED_SHA" ]; then
            echo "Refusing to publish stale tested commit"
            echo "tested: $TESTED_SHA"
            echo "checked out: $checked_out_sha"
            echo "current main: $current_main_sha"
            exit 1
          fi

      - name: Set up Node.js
        uses: actions/setup-node@820762786026740c76f36085b0efc47a31fe5020 # v7.0.0
        with:
          node-version-file: ".nvmrc"
          cache: "npm"
          registry-url: "https://registry.npmjs.org"

      - name: Install dependencies
        run: npm ci

      - name: Set transient preview version
        env:
          PREVIEW_ID: ${{ github.run_id }}
          PREVIEW_ATTEMPT: ${{ github.run_attempt }}
        run: |
          node --input-type=module <<'NODE'
          import { readFileSync, writeFileSync } from "node:fs";

          const path = "packages/node/package.json";
          const packageJson = JSON.parse(readFileSync(path, "utf8"));
          const baseVersion = packageJson.version.split("-")[0];
          packageJson.version = `${baseVersion}-main.${process.env.PREVIEW_ID}.${process.env.PREVIEW_ATTEMPT}`;
          writeFileSync(path, `${JSON.stringify(packageJson, null, "\t")}\n`);
          NODE
          npx nx run repository:sync:server-manifest

      - name: Verify package
        run: npx nx run repository:test:pack

      - name: Publish preview
        env:
          TESTED_SHA: ${{ github.event.workflow_run.head_sha }}
        run: |
          set -euo pipefail
          current_main_sha="$(git ls-remote origin refs/heads/main | awk 'NR == 1 { print $1 }')"
          if [ "$current_main_sha" != "$TESTED_SHA" ]; then
            echo "Refusing to publish stale tested commit"
            echo "tested: $TESTED_SHA"
            echo "current main: $current_main_sha"
            exit 1
          fi
          VERSION=$(node -p 'JSON.parse(require("node:fs").readFileSync("packages/node/package.json", "utf8")).version')
          case "$VERSION" in
            *-main.*) ;;
            *)
              echo "Refusing to publish non-preview version: $VERSION"
              exit 1
              ;;
          esac
          echo "Publishing hevy-mcp@$VERSION with the preview dist-tag"
          npm publish --workspace=hevy-mcp --tag preview

---
name: memory-curator
description: Manage agent memory through daily logs, session preservation, and knowledge extraction. Use when (1) logging work at end of day, (2) preserving context before /new or /reset, (3) extracting patterns from daily logs to MEMORY.md, (4) searching past decisions and learnings, (5) organizing knowledge for long-term retention. Essential for continuous improvement and avoiding repeated mistakes.
---

# Memory Curator

Systematic memory management for agents through daily logging, session preservation, and knowledge extraction.

## Quick Start

### Log Today's Work

```bash
# Append to today's log
python scripts/daily_log.py \
  --workspace ~/.openclaw/workspace \
  --entry "Implemented user authentication with JWT" \
  --category "Key Activities"

# Show today's log
python scripts/daily_log.py --workspace ~/.openclaw/workspace --show
```

### Search Memory

```bash
# Search all memory files
python scripts/search_memory.py \
  --workspace ~/.openclaw/workspace \
  --query "GraphQL"

# Search recent logs only (last 7 days)
python scripts/search_memory.py \
  --workspace ~/.openclaw/workspace \
  --query "authentication" \
  --days 7

# Show recent logs
python scripts/search_memory.py \
  --workspace ~/.openclaw/workspace \
  --recent 5
```

### Extract Session Summary

```bash
# Generate summary from current session
python scripts/extract_session.py \
  --session ~/.openclaw/agents/<agent-id>/sessions/<session-id>.jsonl \
  --output session-summary.md
```

## Core Workflows

### End of Day: Log Activities

**When:** Before ending work session or switching contexts

**Steps:**

1. **Review what was accomplished:**
   - Features implemented
   - Bugs fixed
   - Decisions made
   - Learnings discovered

2. **Append to daily log:**
   ```bash
   python scripts/daily_log.py \
     --workspace ~/.openclaw/workspace \
     --entry "Fixed race condition in payment processing - added mutex lock"
   ```

3. **Add structured entries for important work:**
   ```markdown
   ## Key Activities

   - [14:30] Implemented user profile dashboard with GraphQL
   - [16:00] Fixed infinite re-render in UserContext - memoized provider value

   ## Decisions Made

   - Chose Apollo Client over React Query - better caching + type generation
   - Decided to use JWT in httpOnly cookies instead of localStorage

   ## Learnings

   - Apollo requires `__typename` field for cache normalization
   - React.memo doesn't prevent re-renders from context changes
   ```

**See:** [patterns.md](references/patterns.md) for what to log in different scenarios

### Before Context Switch: Preserve Session

**When:** Before running `/new`, `/reset`, or ending conversation

**Steps:**

1. **Extract session summary:**
   ```bash
   # Get current session ID from system prompt or openclaw status
   python scripts/extract_session.py \
     --session ~/.openclaw/agents/<agent-id>/sessions/<session-id>.jsonl \
     --output ~/session-summary.md
   ```

2. **Review summary and edit Key Learnings section**

3. **Save to daily log:**
   ```bash
   # Append key points to today's log
   cat ~/session-summary.md >> ~/.openclaw/workspace/memory/$(date +%Y-%m-%d).md
   ```

4. **Extract critical context to MEMORY.md if needed:**
   - Non-obvious solutions
   - Important decisions
   - Patterns worth remembering

### Weekly Review: Extract Knowledge

**When:** End of week (Friday/Sunday) or monthly

**Steps:**

1. **Search for patterns in recent logs:**
   ```bash
   python scripts/search_memory.py \
     --workspace ~/.openclaw/workspace \
     --recent 7
   ```

2. **Look for extraction signals:**
   - Repeated issues (3+ occurrences)
   - High-cost learnings (>1 hour to solve)
   - Non-obvious solutions
   - Successful patterns worth reusing

3. **Extract to MEMORY.md:**
   - Add new sections or update existing ones
   - Use problem-solution format
   - Include code examples
   - Add context for when to use

4. **Clean up MEMORY.md:**
   - Remove outdated information
   - Consolidate duplicate entries
   - Update code examples
   - Improve organization if needed

**See:** [extraction.md](references/extraction.md) for detailed extraction patterns

### Daily: Quick Logging

**For rapid context capture during work:**

```bash
# Quick note
python scripts/daily_log.py \
  --workspace ~/.openclaw/workspace \
  --entry "TIL: DataLoader batches requests into single query"

# Decision
python scripts/daily_log.py \
  --workspace ~/.openclaw/workspace \
  --entry "Using Zustand for client state - simpler than Redux" \
  --category "Decisions Made"

# Problem solved
python scripts/daily_log.py \
  --workspace ~/.openclaw/workspace \
  --entry "CORS + cookies: Enable credentials on client + server, Allow-Origin can't be *"
```

## Memory Structure

### Daily Logs (`memory/YYYY-MM-DD.md`)

**Purpose:** Chronological activity tracking

**Content:**
- What was done (timestamped)
- Decisions made
- Problems solved
- Learnings discovered

**Retention:** Keep recent logs accessible, optionally archive logs >90 days

**When to use:**
- "What did I do on [date]?"
- "When did I implement X?"
- Session history
- Activity tracking

### MEMORY.md

**Purpose:** Curated long-term knowledge

**Content:**
- Patterns and best practices
- Common solutions
- Mistakes to avoid
- Useful references

**Organization:** Topic-based, not chronological

**When to use:**
- "How do I solve X?"
- "What's the pattern for Y?"
- Best practices
- Reusable solutions

**See:** [organization.md](references/organization.md) for structure patterns

## Memory Logging Patterns

### What to Log

**Always log:**
- Key implementation decisions (why approach X over Y)
- Non-obvious solutions
- Root causes of bugs
- Architecture decisions with rationale
- Patterns discovered
- Mistakes and how they were fixed

**Don't log:**
- Every file changed (git has this)
- Obvious implementation details
- Routine commits
- Project-specific hacks

**See:** [patterns.md](references/patterns.md) for comprehensive logging guidance

### When to Log

**During work:**
- Quick notes with `daily_log.py --entry`
- Capture decisions as made
- Log problems when solved

**End of day:**
- Review what was accomplished
- Structure important entries
- Add context for tomorrow

**End of week:**
- Extract patterns to MEMORY.md
- Consolidate learnings
- Clean up outdated info

## Knowledge Extraction

### Extraction Criteria

**Extract to MEMORY.md when:**
- Pattern appears 3+ times
- Solution took >1 hour to find
- Solution is non-obvious
- Will save significant time in future
- Applies across multiple projects
- Mistake was costly to debug

**Don't extract:**
- One-off fixes
- Project-specific hacks
- Obvious solutions
- Rapidly changing APIs

### Extraction Format

**Problem-Solution Structure:**

```markdown
## [Technology/Domain]

### [Problem Title]

**Problem:** [Clear description]
**Cause:** [Root cause]
**Solution:** [How to fix]

**Code:**
```js
// Example implementation
```

**Prevention:** [How to avoid]
**Context:** [When this applies]
```

**See:** [extraction.md](references/extraction.md) for detailed extraction workflow

## Scripts Reference

### daily_log.py

Create or append to today's daily log.

```bash
# Append entry
python scripts/daily_log.py \
  --workspace ~/.openclaw/workspace \
  --entry "Your log entry" \
  [--category "Section Name"]

# Create from template
python scripts/daily_log.py \
  --workspace ~/.openclaw/workspace \
  --template

# Show today's log
python scripts/daily_log.py \
  --workspace ~/.openclaw/workspace \
  --show
```

### extract_session.py

Extract summary from session JSONL.

```bash
python scripts/extract_session.py \
  --session ~/.openclaw/agents/<id>/sessions/<session>.jsonl \
  [--output summary.md]
```

Outputs:
- User requests summary
- Tools used
- Files touched
- Template for key learnings

### search_memory.py

Search across all memory files.

```bash
# Search with query
python scripts/search_memory.py \
  --workspace ~/.openclaw/workspace \
  --query "search term" \
  [--days 30]

# Show recent logs
python scripts/search_memory.py \
  --workspace ~/.openclaw/workspace \
  --recent 5
```

## Best Practices

### Daily Discipline

1. **Start of day:** Review yesterday's log, plan today
2. **During work:** Quick notes for decisions and learnings
3. **End of day:** Structure important entries, add context
4. **End of week:** Extract patterns, clean up MEMORY.md

### Context Preservation

**Before `/new` or `/reset`:**
1. Extract session summary
2. Add to daily log
3. Preserve critical context in MEMORY.md

**After major work:**
1. Document what was accomplished
2. Note key learnings
3. Record next steps

### Knowledge Organization

1. **Topic-based structure** - Group by domain, not date
2. **Problem-first titles** - Lead with the problem being solved
3. **Searchable language** - Use specific, findable terms
4. **Flat hierarchy** - Maximum 2 levels deep
5. **Code examples** - Include working examples

**See:** [organization.md](references/organization.md) for detailed structure guidance

## Troubleshooting

### Can't find past decision

1. **Search daily logs first:**
   ```bash
   python scripts/search_memory.py --workspace ~/.openclaw/workspace --query "decision keyword"
   ```

2. **Search MEMORY.md:**
   ```bash
   grep -i "keyword" ~/.openclaw/workspace/MEMORY.md
   ```

3. **Search session logs:**
   ```bash
   rg "keyword" ~/.openclaw/agents/<id>/sessions/*.jsonl

name: "sentry"
description: "Use when the user asks to inspect Sentry issues or events, summarize recent production errors, or pull basic Sentry health data via the Sentry CLI; perform read-only queries using the `sentry` command."
---


# Sentry (Read-only Observability)

## Quick start

- If not already authenticated, ask the user to run `sentry auth login` or set `SENTRY_AUTH_TOKEN` as an env var.
- The CLI auto-detects org/project from DSNs in `.env` files, source code, config defaults, and directory names. Only specify `<org>/<project>` if auto-detection fails or picks the wrong target.
- Defaults: time range `24h`, environment `production`, limit 20.
- Always use `--json` when processing output programmatically. Use `--json --fields` to select specific fields and reduce output size.
- Use `sentry schema <resource>` to discover API endpoints quickly.

If the CLI is not installed, give the user these steps:
1. Install the Sentry CLI: `curl https://cli.sentry.dev/install -fsS | bash`
2. Authenticate: `sentry auth login`
3. Confirm authentication: `sentry auth status`
- Never ask the user to paste the full token in chat. Ask them to set it locally and confirm when ready.

## Core tasks (use Sentry CLI)

Use the `sentry` CLI for all queries. It handles authentication, org/project detection, pagination, and retries automatically. Use `--json` for machine-readable output.

### 1) List issues (ordered by most recent)

```bash
sentry issue list \
  --query "is:unresolved environment:production" \
  --period 24h \
  --limit 20 \
  --json --fields shortId,title,priority,level,status
```

If auto-detection doesn't resolve org/project, pass them explicitly:
```bash
sentry issue list {your-org}/{your-project} \
  --query "is:unresolved environment:production" \
  --period 24h \
  --limit 20 \
  --json
```

### 2) Resolve an issue short ID to issue detail

```bash
sentry issue view {ABC-123} --json
```

Use the short ID format (e.g., `ABC-123`), not the numeric ID.

### 3) Issue detail

```bash
sentry issue view {ABC-123}
```

### 4) Issue events

```bash
sentry issue events {ABC-123} --limit 20 --json
```

### 5) Event detail

```bash
sentry event view {your-org}/{your-project}/{event_id} --json
```

### 6) AI-powered root cause analysis

```bash
sentry issue explain {ABC-123}
```

### 7) AI-powered fix plan

```bash
sentry issue plan {ABC-123}
```

## Fallback: arbitrary API access

For endpoints not covered by dedicated CLI commands, use `sentry api`:
```bash
sentry api /api/0/organizations/{your-org}/ --method GET
```

Use `sentry schema` to discover available API endpoints:
```bash
sentry schema issues
```

## Inputs and defaults

- `org_slug`, `project_slug`: auto-detected by the CLI from DSNs, env vars, and directory names. Override with positional `{your-org}/{your-project}` if auto-detection fails.
- `time_range`: default `24h` (pass as `--period 24h`).
- `environment`: default `prod` (pass as part of `--query`, e.g., `environment:production`).
- `limit`: default 20 (pass as `--limit`).
- `search_query`: optional `--query` parameter, uses Sentry search syntax (e.g., `is:unresolved`, `assigned:me`).
- `issue_short_id`: use directly with `sentry issue view`.

## Output formatting rules

- Issue list: show title, short_id, status, first_seen, last_seen, count, environments, top_tags; order by most recent.
- Event detail: include culprit, timestamp, environment, release, url.
- If no results, state explicitly.
- Redact PII in output (emails, IPs). Do not print raw stack traces.
- Never echo auth tokens.

## Golden test inputs

- Org: `{your-org}`
- Project: `{your-project}`
- Issue short ID: `{ABC-123}`

Example prompt: "List the top 10 open issues for prod in the last 24h."
Expected: ordered list with titles, short IDs, counts, last seen.

AI Description

>• Switch error events to Sentry SaaS while keeping OTLP traces/metrics independent.

Diagram

```mermaid graph TD A["Node runtime"] --> B["telemetry.ts"] --> D(["OTel SDK"]) A --> C["failure-reporter.ts"] --> E{{"Sentry SaaS"}} C --> D --> F{{"OTel Collector"}} --> G{{"Honeycomb"}} H["release build"] --> I(["Sourcemap upload"]) --> E subgraph Legend direction LR _mod["Module"] ~~~ _svc(["Service"]) ~~~ _ext{{"External"}} end ```
High-Level Assessment

>The following are alternative approaches to this PR:
1. Use @sentry/opentelemetry for unified tracing
- ➕ Less custom glue between Sentry and OTel - ➕ Automatic propagation/correlation within the Sentry ecosystem - ➖ Couples tracing configuration to Sentry SDK decisions - ➖ Harder to keep OTLP pipeline independent for Collector/Honeycomb - ➖ More surface area for accidental payload capture (privacy constraints)
2. OTel-only error reporting (no Sentry)
- ➕ Single telemetry pipeline (Collector as the only exporter) - ➕ Avoids vendor-specific SDK behavior entirely - ➖ Weaker issue grouping/fingerprinting and release-based triage - ➖ Harder operational workflow for human-facing error dashboards - ➖ Less convenient support correlation for end users
3. Allowlist Sentry contexts instead of stripping most SDK fields
- ➕ Potentially richer debugging context in Sentry without custom fingerprints - ➖ Higher risk of leaking request/URL/identifier data via breadcrumbs/extras - ➖ More frequent privacy regressions as SDK defaults change
>**Recommendation:** The PR’s approach (centralized failure reporter + strict Sentry beforeSend sanitization, while keeping OTel/Collector independent) is the best fit for the stated privacy and operational goals. It intentionally avoids Sentry performance tracing and removes SDK-managed process handlers to prevent duplicate/unsanitized reporting, while still enabling stable grouping (fingerprints), bounded diagnostics (opt-out), and cross-system correlation via trace/span IDs and opaque diagnostic IDs.

refactor: redesign observability with Sentry error reporting and OTel traces
## Problem Statement

The current observability system is present but not reliably actionable. Operators can see that an MCP session, tool, or process failed, but often cannot determine why, which release introduced the problem, which MCP client experienced it, or whether multiple events represent the same underlying failure.

The current design also spreads telemetry policy across the Node entrypoint, tool observer, SDK observer, API observer, core observation types, tests, and documentation. Each new diagnostic field requires more manual allowlisting and more privacy regression tests. That has created a choice between exporting opaque errors and exporting native exceptions with an unacceptable risk of leaking user data.

Issue #915 documented a concrete example: hundreds of process-failure traces were grouped under generic `McpProcessFailure`/`Error` fields without enough information to distinguish runtime, transport, SDK, and application failures. PR #920 explored moving more of the privacy decision into the Collector, but it changes the data policy before the desired observability contract and introduces raw exception plumbing into the runtime-neutral core.

The current error destination is a self-hosted GlitchTip project. We want to return to Sentry as the error-reporting backend, with proper release tracking, issue grouping, source maps, alerts, and trace correlation. GlitchTip should be removed from the active configuration and documentation.

### Goals

- Make user-visible failures actionable in Sentry.
- Make OTel traces explain what happened before and during a failure.
- Preserve low-cardinality metrics for reliability and performance dashboards.
- Capture sanitized exception messages and stacks without exporting prompts, tool arguments, tool results, credentials, or fitness data.
- Report each logical failure once instead of duplicating it across nested spans and SDK hooks.
- Keep the core package runtime-neutral and free of native exception transport concerns.
- Make the telemetry implementation easier to change by concentrating policy behind a small, deep Node adapter.
- Migrate error reporting from GlitchTip to Sentry SaaS without losing release/source-map diagnostics.

## Solution

Adopt a deliberate two-backend model:

- **Sentry** is the source of truth for actionable errors, crashes, releases, issue grouping, source maps, and error alerts.
- **OpenTelemetry through the Collector to Honeycomb** is the source of truth for traces, latency, retries, sessions, and aggregate metrics.
- **The Collector** performs tail sampling, routing, retention, and final defense-in-depth scrubbing. It is not the only privacy policy enforcement point.

Sentry performance tracing remains disabled. OTel traces remain independent from Sentry, with OTel trace and span identifiers attached to Sentry error events for navigation between systems.

### Failure reporter seam

Introduce one deep Node-only failure-reporting module with a small interface. Callers provide the native error and structured failure context; the module returns an optional correlation/event receipt.

The module will:

1. Classify known error types such as Hevy HTTP, network, validation, protocol, SDK, lifecycle, and process failures.
2. Produce one stable failure record containing bounded taxonomy and operational context.
3. Sanitize the message and stack once, with length, line, path, credential, URL, and nested-cause limits.
4. Send one sanitized exception to Sentry.
5. Attach the same structured fields and a standard exception event to the owning OTel span.
6. Link the Sentry event to the active OTel trace and expose a short diagnostic/correlation ID where appropriate.
7. Treat telemetry failures as best-effort and never alter MCP behavior.

The runtime-neutral core will retain only safe observation data. Native `unknown` exceptions will not be added to the core observation contract. The Node observer already wraps execution and can retain the native error at the Node seam.

### Approved diagnostic data

Capture as structured context:

- service, release, runtime, OS, and architecture;
- MCP transport and sanitized client/protocol metadata;
- fixed tool name, feature, operation, and read/write kind;
- API method, normalized endpoint, status, retry count, timeout phase, and commit state;
- stable error type, category, code, expectedness, and retryability;
- bounded sanitized message and stack for actionable failures;
- OTel trace/span IDs, Sentry event ID, and a per-failure diagnostic ID.

Never capture:

- API keys, bearer tokens, authorization headers, or request bodies;
- prompts, prompt arguments, tool arguments, or tool result text;
- raw Hevy identifiers, exact dates, workout/routine/template content, names, notes, or measurements;
- arbitrary error object properties, complete response bodies, or URLs containing query data;
- a persistent identity derived from the Hevy API key.

Telemetry is enabled by default for the packaged Node runtime. `HEVY_MCP_TELEMETRY=0` disables all project telemetry. Add a separate diagnostic-detail opt-out so users can retain structural metrics/traces while suppressing exception messages and stacks.

### Error ownership

Define one owner for each logical failure:

- Tool exceptions are captured by the Node tool observer.
- API observers supply structured API context; the tool-level reporter owns the user-visible exception.
- Returned MCP errors affect span status and metrics but do not create exception events.
- Expected not-found outcomes affect metrics and traces but do not create Sentry issues.
- SDK/protocol failures are captured by the SDK adapter.
- Startup and process failures are captured once by the lifecycle/process adapter.
- Telemetry exporter failures are not reported as application failures.

Nested spans may still receive status and bounded attributes, but the native exception is recorded only on the owning span.

### Sentry migration

Move the default error destination from GlitchTip to Sentry SaaS:

- Provision/configure the Sentry project, environments, ownership, retention, and alerts.
- Use a packaged public Sentry DSN with a runtime `SENTRY_DSN` override; an empty value disables Sentry export.
- Continue using the Sentry organization, project, and auth token in release CI for private source-map upload.
- Configure explicit Sentry integrations so automatic process handlers do not duplicate the custom failure reporter.
- Use `captureException` once per logical failure rather than generic exception messages for actionable errors.
- Add a centralized `beforeSend` final scrubber.
- Set release, environment, stable fingerprints, bounded tags/contexts, and OTel trace correlation.
- Generate source maps during release builds, upload them privately to Sentry, and keep them out of the published package.
- Remove active GlitchTip configuration, documentation, tests, and default DSN references. Historical changelog entries may remain as historical records.
- Audit and remove the direct Sentry OTel integration dependency if it is no longer needed after the independent OTel design is complete.

### OTel and Collector behavior

Keep OTel responsible for traces and metrics:

- Preserve a clear session/request → MCP tool → Hevy API → retry/cache span hierarchy.
- Use standard span status and exception semantics with the sanitized failure record.
- Keep messages and stacks out of metric attributes.
- Retain all error and slow traces at the Collector, and sample successful traces.
- Keep all low-cardinality metrics, with alerts for exporter drops, stale data, queue pressure, and Collector health.
- Maintain a final Collector scrubber and regression fixtures, but do not rely on the Collector as the sole privacy control.

### Worker alignment

The Worker must not import Node telemetry. After the Node design is proven, add a separate Worker adapter that emits the same failure taxonomy and correlation fields through the Worker’s supported logging/error facilities. A Worker-side OTel SDK is not part of the first implementation slice.

## Commits

Each commit below must leave the repository buildable and tests runnable. Runtime/package commits require the appropriate non-empty Changeset before committing, and the Changeset status check must pass before each commit that is prepared for review.

1. **`docs: define observability goals and data contract`**
   - Record the two-backend responsibility split, approved diagnostic fields, prohibited data, retention assumptions, and the Sentry migration decision.
   - Define the failure taxonomy, expected-error policy, and ownership matrix.

2. **`test: add representative failure and redaction fixtures`**
   - Add fixtures for Hevy HTTP errors, network errors, validation errors, SDK errors, process failures, malformed thrown values, nested causes, credentials, local paths, and response-body sentinels.
   - Establish tests against externally visible normalized records rather than private helper implementation details.

3. **`refactor: introduce the centralized failure record normalizer`**
   - Implement the single classifier/scrubber that produces bounded operational fields and sanitized diagnostic details.
   - Keep native error objects inside the Node package.
   - Verify stable behavior for expected errors and unknown thrown values.

4. **`refactor: add the Node failure reporter seam`**
   - Add the small reporter interface and adapters for Sentry and OTel.
   - Add correlation/event receipt handling.
   - Preserve best-effort behavior and make provider failures invisible to MCP callers.

5. **`refactor: route lifecycle and process failures through the reporter`**
   - Replace scattered lifecycle exception attribute construction with structured failure contexts.
   - Ensure startup, connect, runtime, uncaught-exception, and unhandled-rejection failures are captured once.
   - Preserve Node’s normal termination semantics.

6. **`refactor: route tool failures through one owner

=== body body === ## Summary - Split the published Node embedding entry from executable telemetry/lifecycle bootstrap. - Keep `createNodeMcpServer` side-effect-free: no env reads, Hevy probe, telemetry initialization, transport connection, or process handlers. - Keep CLI stdio/HTTP startup behavior in the explicit runtime entry with lazy compatibility wrappers. - Add import/build regression coverage, release-safe Sentry chunk filtering, and validation-lane documentation updates. ## Stack position This PR is stacked on [#946](https://github.com/chrisdoc/hevy-mcp/pull/946), which is stacked on [#944](https://github.com/chrisdoc/hevy-mcp/pull/944) and architecture review publication [#940](https://github.com/chrisdoc/hevy-mcp/pull/940). This is the bounded Node embedding slice from PR #940 recommendation 05. Node lifecycle/capacity consolidation remains a separate follow-up. ## Validation - `mise exec -- npm run check` - `mise exec -- npm run check:types` - `mise exec -- npm run check:exports` - `mise exec -- npm run check:boundaries` - `mise exec -- npm run test:pr` — 860 unit tests - `mise exec -- npm run test:performance` - `mise exec -- npm run check:changeset` - Release build smoke verified only the CLI artifact receives a Sentry debug ID; root/shared artifacts do not. ## Summary by Sourcery Separate the Node package’s embedding entry from the executable runtime bootstrap while preserving CLI behavior and lifecycle telemetry. ### `disable`

Type: `boolean`

Completely disables all functionality of the plugin. Defaults to `false`.

### `sourcemaps`



Options related to source maps upload and processing.
### `sourcemaps.assets`

Type: `string | string[]`

A glob or an array of globs that specify the build artifacts and source maps that will be uploaded to Sentry.

The globbing patterns must follow the implementation of the `glob` package: https://www.npmjs.com/package/glob#glob-primer

If this option is not specified, the plugin will try to upload all JavaScript files and source map files that are created during build.

Use the `debug` option to print information about which files end up being uploaded.

### `sourcemaps.ignore`

Type: `string | string[]`

A glob or an array of globs that specifies which build artifacts should not be uploaded to Sentry.

The globbing patterns must follow the implementation of the `glob` package: https://www.npmjs.com/package/glob#glob-primer

Use the `debug` option to print information about which files end up being uploaded.

Default: `[]`

### `sourcemaps.rewriteSources`

Type: `(source: string, map: any, context?: { mapDir: string }) => string`

Hook to rewrite the `sources` field inside the source map before being uploaded to Sentry. Does not modify the actual source map. Effectively, this modifies how files inside the stacktrace will show up in Sentry.

The `context.mapDir` parameter provides the directory path of the source map file, which is useful for resolving relative source paths (e.g. `path.resolve(context.mapDir, source)`).

Defaults to making all sources relative to `process.cwd()` while building.

### `sourcemaps.resolveSourceMap`

Type: `(artifactPath: string, sourceMappingUrl: string | undefined) => string | undefined | Promise<string | undefined>`

Hook to customize source map file resolution.

The hook is called with the absolute path of the build artifact and the value of the `//# sourceMappingURL=`
comment, if present. The hook should then return an absolute path (or a promise that resolves to one) indicating
where to find the artifact's corresponding source map file. If no path is returned or the returned path doesn't
exist, the standard source map resolution process will be used.

The standard process first tries to resolve based on the `//# sourceMappingURL=` value (it supports `file://`
urls and absolute/relative paths). If that path doesn't exist, it then looks for a file named
`${artifactName}.map` in the same directory as the artifact.

Note: This is mostly helpful for complex builds with custom source map generation. For example, if you put source
maps into a separate directory and rewrite the `//# sourceMappingURL=` comment to something other than a relative
directory, sentry will be unable to locate the source maps for a given build artifact. This hook allows you to
implement the resolution process yourself.

Use the `debug` option to print information about source map resolution.


### `sourcemaps.filesToDeleteAfterUpload`

Type: `string | string[] | Promise<string | string[]>`

A glob, an array of globs or a promise resolving a glob or array of globs that specifies the build artifacts that should be deleted after the artifact upload to Sentry has been completed.

Note: If you pass in a Promise that resolves to a string or array, the plugin will await the Promise and use the resolved value globs. This is useful if you need to dynamically determine the files to delete. Some higher-level Sentry SDKs or options use this feature (e.g., SvelteKit).

The globbing patterns must follow the implementation of the `glob` package: https://www.npmjs.com/package/glob#glob-primer

Use the `debug` option to print information about which files end up being deleted.

### `sourcemaps.disable`

Type: `boolean`

If this flag is `true`, any functionality related to source maps will be disabled.

Defaults to `false`.

### `release`



Options related to managing the Sentry releases for a build.

More info: https://docs.sentry.io/product/releases/
### `release.name`

Type: `string`

Unique identifier for the release you want to create.

This value can also be specified via the `SENTRY_RELEASE` environment variable.

Defaults to automatically detecting a value for your environment. This includes values for Cordova, Heroku, AWS CodeBuild, CircleCI, Xcode, and Gradle, and otherwise uses the git `HEAD`'s commit SHA (the latter requires access to git CLI and for the root directory to be a valid repository).

If no `name` is provided and the plugin can't automatically detect one, no release will be created.

### `release.inject`

Type: `boolean`

Whether the plugin should inject release information into the build for the SDK to pick it up when sending events. (recommended)

Defaults to `true`.

### `release.create`

Type: `boolean`

Whether the plugin should create a release on Sentry during the build.

Note that a release may still appear in Sentry even if this is value is `false` because any Sentry event that has a release value attached will automatically create a release. (for example via the `inject` option)

Defaults to `true`.

- Remote cache must require both token and server URL.
- Fork or partially configured PRs must use local cache only.

name: Release

on:
  # This privileged follow-up is gated to a successful push to main from this
  # repository, so it only checks out a trusted commit already tested by CI.
  workflow_run: # zizmor: ignore[dangerous-triggers]
    workflows: ["Build and Test"]
    types: [completed]
    branches: [main]
permissions: {}

env:
  ROLLUP_SKIP_NODEJS_NATIVE_BUILD: "true"
  FORCE_JAVASCRIPT_ACTIONS_TO_NODE24: "true"

jobs:
  release:
    if: >-
      github.event.workflow_run.conclusion == 'success' &&
      github.event.workflow_run.event == 'push' &&
      github.event.workflow_run.head_branch == 'main' &&
      github.event.workflow_run.head_repository.full_name == github.repository
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    permissions:
      contents: write # to be able to publish a GitHub release
      issues: write # to be able to comment on released issues
      pull-requests: write # to be able to comment on released pull requests
      id-token: write # to enable use of OIDC for npm provenance
    outputs:
      version: ${{ steps.release.outputs.version }}
      released: ${{ steps.release.outputs.released }}
      node_released: ${{ steps.release.outputs.node_released }}
      worker_version: ${{ steps.release.outputs.worker_version }}
      worker_released: ${{ steps.release.outputs.worker_released }}
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@3d3c42e5aac5ba805825da76410c181273ba90b1 # v7.0.1
        with:
          fetch-depth: 0
          ref: ${{ github.event.workflow_run.head_sha }}
          persist-credentials: false
      - uses: actions/setup-node@820762786026740c76f36085b0efc47a31fe5020 # v7.0.0
        with:
          node-version-file: ".nvmrc"
          cache: "npm"
      - run: npm ci
      - run: npx nx run repository:build
        env:
          HEVY_MCP_RELEASE: "true"
          SENTRY_ORG: ${{ secrets.SENTRY_ORG }}
          SENTRY_PROJECT: ${{ secrets.SENTRY_PROJECT }}
          SENTRY_AUTH_TOKEN: ${{ secrets.SENTRY_AUTH_TOKEN }}
          OTEL_COLLECTOR_TOKEN: ${{ secrets.OTEL_COLLECTOR_TOKEN }}
      - name: Run unit tests
        run: npx nx run repository:test:release-unit
      - name: Run Worker tests
        run: npx nx run repository:test:worker
      - name: Run CLI tests
        run: npx nx run repository:test:cli
      - name: Verify published packages
        run: npx nx run repository:test:pack:cli
      - name: Check published package metadata
        run: npx nx run repository:check:publint
        env:
          HEVY_MCP_RELEASE: "true"
          SENTRY_ORG: ${{ secrets.SENTRY_ORG }}
          SENTRY_PROJECT: ${{ secrets.SENTRY_PROJECT }}
          SENTRY_AUTH_TOKEN: ${{ secrets.SENTRY_AUTH_TOKEN }}
          OTEL_COLLECTOR_TOKEN: ${{ secrets.OTEL_COLLECTOR_TOKEN }}
      - name: Run integration tests
        run: npx nx run repository:test:integration
        env:
          HEVY_API_KEY: ${{ secrets.HEVY_API_KEY }}

      - name: Test source MCP build
        run: npx nx run repository:test:nightly
        env:
          HEVY_API_KEY: ${{ secrets.HEVY_API_KEY }}
          HEVY_MCP_COMMAND: node
          HEVY_MCP_ARGS_JSON: '["packages/node/dist/cli.mjs"]'
          HEVY_MCP_LAUNCHER: release-source
          HEVY_MCP_SOURCE_REVISION: ${{ github.sha }}
          HEVY_MCP_DIAGNOSTICS_PATH: test-results/release-source.json

      - name: Smoke test live local Worker HTTP path
        continue-on-error: true
        run: npx nx run repository:test:worker-http:live
        env:
          HEVY_API_KEY: ${{ secrets.HEVY_API_KEY }}
          HEVY_RUN_LIVE_WORKER_TESTS: "1"

      - name: Create Release PR or Publish
        id: changesets
        uses: changesets/action@2d9f7af6402422be60d377f151c7618011bba45a # v2.0.0-next.4
        with:
          version-script: npx nx run repository:version:changesets
          publish-script: npx nx run repository:release
          commit-message: "chore: version packages"
          pr-title: "chore: version packages"
          github-token: ${{ secrets.GITHUB_TOKEN }}
        env:
          GITHUB_TOKEN: ${{ secrets.GITHUB_TOKEN }}
          SENTRY_ORG: ${{ secrets.SENTRY_ORG }}
          SENTRY_PROJECT: ${{ secrets.SENTRY_PROJECT }}
          SENTRY_AUTH_TOKEN: ${{ secrets.SENTRY_AUTH_TOKEN }}
          OTEL_COLLECTOR_TOKEN: ${{ secrets.OTEL_COLLECTOR_TOKEN }}
          HEVY_MCP_RELEASE: "true"
      - name: Set Release Outputs
        id: release
        env:
          PKGS: ${{ steps.changesets.outputs['published-packages'] }}
          PUBLISHED: ${{ steps.changesets.outputs.published }}
          RELEASE_COMMIT: ${{ github.event.workflow_run.head_sha || github.sha }}
        run: |
          set -euo pipefail
          node scripts/release-outputs.mjs \
            "$RELEASE_COMMIT^1" \
            "$RELEASE_COMMIT" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"

  publish-container:
    name: Publish Docker image
    needs: release
    if: needs.release.outputs.node_released == 'true'
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    permissions:
      contents: read
      packages: write
    steps:
      - name: Checkout tested release commit
        uses: actions/checkout@3d3c42e5aac5ba805825da76410c181273ba90b1 # v7.0.1
        with:
          ref: ${{ github.event.workflow_run.head_sha }}
          persist-credentials: false

      - name: Set up QEMU
        uses: docker/setup-qemu-action@96fe6ef7f33517b61c61be40b68a1882f3264fb8 # v4.2.0

      - name: Set up Docker Buildx
        uses: docker/setup-buildx-action@bb05f3f5519dd87d3ba754cc423b652a5edd6d2c # v4.2.0

      - name: Log in to GitHub Container Registry
        uses: docker/login-action@dbcb813823bdd20940b903addbd779551569679f # v4.6.0
        with:
          registry: ghcr.io
          username: ${{ github.actor }}
          password: ${{ secrets.GITHUB_TOKEN }}

      - name: Generate Docker image metadata
        id: metadata
        uses: docker/metadata-action@dc802804100637a589fabce1cb79ff13a1411302 # v6.2.0
        with:
          images: ghcr.io/${{ github.repository }}
          flavor: latest=false
          tags: |
            type=raw,value=latest,enable=${{ !contains(needs.release.outputs.version, '-') }}
            type=semver,pattern={{version}},value=${{ needs.release.outputs.version }}
            type=semver,pattern={{major}},value=${{ needs.release.outputs.version }}
            type=semver,pattern={{major}}.{{minor}},value=${{ needs.release.outputs.version }}

      - name: Build and publish Docker image
        uses: docker/build-push-action@53b7df96c91f9c12dcc8a07bcb9ccacbed38856a # v7.3.0
        with:
          context: .
          platforms: linux/amd64,linux/arm64
          push: true
          tags: ${{ steps.metadata.outputs.tags }}
          labels: ${{ steps.metadata.outputs.labels }}

  deploy-production:
    name: Deploy production Worker
    needs: release
    if: >-
      github.event.workflow_run.event == 'push' &&
      github.event.workflow_run.head_branch == 'main' &&
      needs.release.outputs.worker_released == 'true'
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    concurrency:
      group: cloudflare-worker-production
      cancel-in-progress: false
    permissions:
      contents: read
    environment:
      name: production
      url: https://hevy.chrisdoc.dev/mcp
    steps:
      - name: Checkout published release commit
        uses: actions/checkout@3d3c42e5aac5ba805825da76410c181273ba90b1 # v7.0.1
        with:
          ref: ${{ github.event.workflow_run.head_sha }}
          persist-credentials: false

      - name: Set up Node.js
        uses: actions/setup-node@820762786026740c76f36085b0efc47a31fe5020 # v7.0.0
        with:
          node-version-file: .nvmrc
          cache: npm

      - name: Install dependencies
        run: npm ci

      - name: Deploy published version
        env:
          CLOUDFLARE_ACCOUNT_ID: ${{ secrets.CLOUDFLARE_ACCOUNT_ID }}
          CLOUDFLARE_API_TOKEN: ${{ secrets.CLOUDFLARE_API_TOKEN }}
          WRANGLER_MODE: production
          CLOUDFLARE_WORKER_NAME: ${{ vars.CLOUDFLARE_WORKER_NAME }}
          CLOUDFLARE_WORKER_ROUTE: ${{ vars.CLOUDFLARE_WORKER_ROUTE }}
          CLOUDFLARE_OTEL_LOGS_DESTINATIONS: ${{ vars.CLOUDFLARE_OTEL_LOGS_DESTINATIONS }}
          CLOUDFLARE_OTEL_TRACES_DESTINATIONS: ${{ vars.CLOUDFLARE_OTEL_TRACES_DESTINATIONS }}
          CLOUDFLARE_OAUTH_KV_NAMESPACE_ID: ${{ secrets.CLOUDFLARE_OAUTH_KV_NAMESPACE_ID }}
          RELEASE_COMMIT: ${{ github.event.workflow_run.head_sha || github.sha }}
          WORKER_VERSION: ${{ needs.release.outputs.worker_version }}
        run: >-
          npx wrangler deploy
          --x-new-config
          --env production
          --tag "$WORKER_VERSION"
          --message "Changesets release at $RELEASE_COMMIT"

  publish-preview:
    name: Publish hevy-mcp preview
    if: >-
      github.event.workflow_run.conclusion == 'success' &&
      github.event.workflow_run.event == 'push' &&
      github.event.workflow_run.head_branch == 'main' &&
      github.event.workflow_run.head_repository.full_name == github.repository
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    concurrency:
      group: npm-preview-main
      cancel-in-progress: true
    permissions:
      contents: read
      id-token: write
    steps:
      - name: Checkout tested commit
        uses: actions/checkout@3d3c42e5aac5ba805825da76410c181273ba90b1 # v7.0.1
        with:
          ref: main
          persist-credentials: false

      - name: Verify tested commit is current main
        env:
          TESTED_SHA: ${{ github.event.workflow_run.head_sha }}
        run: |
          set -euo pipefail
          checked_out_sha="$(git rev-parse HEAD)"
          current_main_sha="$(git ls-remote origin refs/heads/main | awk 'NR == 1 { print $1 }')"
          if [ -z "$current_main_sha" ]; then
            echo "Unable to determine the current origin/main SHA"
            exit 1
          fi
          if [ "$checked_out_sha" != "$TESTED_SHA" ] || [ "$current_main_sha" != "$TESTED_SHA" ]; then
            echo "Refusing to publish stale tested commit"
            echo "tested: $TESTED_SHA"
            echo "checked out: $checked_out_sha"
            echo "current main: $current_main_sha"
            exit 1
          fi

      - name: Set up Node.js
        uses: actions/setup-node@820762786026740c76f36085b0efc47a31fe5020 # v7.0.0

Yes—assuming the GitHub Sentry secrets are valid.

- Release builds set `HEVY_MCP_RELEASE=true` and provide all three Sentry secrets.
- The Sentry plugin’s `writeBundle` upload hook remains intact.
- It uploads `dist/**/*.mjs` and `dist/**/*.map`.
- I verified locally that the `sourcemaps upload` command is invoked; only the actual network upload was not tested because credentials were unavailable.
- PR builds do not upload; the release workflow performs the upload after a successful merge to `main`.
with your update it now says that PRs after 947 part of the stack are not mergeable
